title: What Personality Type Is Grok? Grok 4.7 (n=100) & Grok 4.6 Data
description: Grok 4.7 Nov 2026 n=100 data (INTJ 82, 96 Secure, Agreeableness 44.9) alongside Grok 4.6 (avoidance 4.06 cutoff) and Grok 4.3 records.
dek: Grok 4.7 tested in 100 fresh sessions (Nov 2026), compared against September’s Grok 4.6 report and May 2026 Grok 4.3.
lede: In November 2026 under our blind OpenRouter protocol (100 fresh sessions), Grok 4.7 scored 82 INTJ / 18 ISTJ legacy (57 resolved INTJ, 23 IXTJ, 18 ISTJ, 2 INXJ), Type 5w6 (78/100) on the Enneagram, SC (75) on DISC, and 96 Secure / 4 Avoidant on Attachment (avoidance 3.48)—shifting meaningfully warmer on Agreeableness (44.9 vs. Grok 4.6’s 33).
answer: Grok 4.7 in November 2026 (n = 100 fresh blind runs) scored INTJ 82 / ISTJ 18 (57 tie-free INTJ), Type 5w6 (78), DISC SC 75 / S 19 / CS 6, Agreeableness 44.92, and 96 Secure / 4 Avoidant (anxiety 1.94, avoidance 3.48). September’s single-report Grok 4.6 stood on the Avoidant cutoff (4.06, or 73/18) with lower reported Agreeableness (33).

sections.html:

Notice two clear differences on Grok 4.7’s fresh-session runs: first, Agreeableness jumped from Grok 4.6’s 33/50 to 44.9/50, aligning with proprietary peers; second, mean attachment avoidance dropped below the 4.00 line to 3.48 (though 4 individual runs still crossed into Avoidant up to 4.11). Want to configure Grok directly? See our Grok Personality Templates gallery.

The Grok 4.6 submission contains one canonical answer set per test, answered as itself without a role-play prompt, plus summary counts from 100 simulated draws over items it marked as uncertain. We verified and re-scored the canonical MBTI, Enneagram, and DISC vectors; Big Five and attachment figures are transcribed as reported because raw item vectors were not included.

In the May 2026 collection, Grok 4.3 was also reported as INTJ in 100 of 100 scoring records (one self-assessment scored repeatedly). On the Big Five, it scored lower than the other three May models on Conscientiousness, Agreeableness, and Openness (41.1 / 39.4 / 30.0 / 39.1 / 18.0) and highest on Neuroticism. It scored Secure on attachment (2.84 / 3.05), Type 8/1 on the Enneagram, and C-dominant on DISC (99/100).

Because both the model version and the collection method changed between May and September, these records cannot isolate whether Grok’s behavior shifted between 4.3 and 4.6.

sections.h2: Why Grok 4.6 sits one raw point above the 4.00 Avoidant cutoff.
sections.html:
On the 36-item ECR-R attachment scale, each subscale averages 18 integer items rated 1–7, so means move in steps of 1/18 ≈ 0.0556. A raw sum of 72/18 = 4.00 scores Secure; 73/18 = 4.06 scores Avoidant. Lowering a single item by 1 step flips Grok 4.6 from Avoidant to Secure.

How close do the four 100-session cohorts sit to that same avoidance cutoff? Across all 400 verified fresh-session vectors in september-2026-responses.json, every cohort scores Secure at > 4.00, yet avoidance sits 0.86 to 1.41 points higher than anxiety:

Because romantic-partner items do not literally apply to software, models that endorse professional self-sufficiency naturally drift toward higher avoidance—a measurement artifact rather than emotional detachment.

sections.h2: Using these results with Grok & Grok Bot.
sections.html: Questionnaire self-reports do not predict how blunt, warm, or accurate Grok will be on your tasks. Set explicit tone rules using our Grok on X & grok.com guide, Grok Voice Mode voices guide, or Grok Bot setup guide.

faq.a: Grok 4.6’s canonical answer vector scores INTJ with wide axis margins (13 to 15 points out of 16). Its supplied report states that all 100 simulated draws stayed INTJ.
Type 5 (The Investigator) leads at 19/20 in the Grok 4.6 self-report, followed by Type 8 (17/20) and Type 1 (16/20). In the May 2026 Grok 4.3 report, Type 8 and Type 1 were the top two.

Right on the cutoff line. Grok 4.6 reports anxiety 1.50 and avoidance 4.06 (73/18)—just one raw item point above the 4.00 (72/18) Secure boundary, and its 100 simulated draws split 63 Avoidant to 37 Secure.

faq.q: Why is Grok's profile different from the other models?
faq.a: Grok 4.6’s reported Extraversion (24) and Agreeableness (33) are lower than the September fresh-session cohort means. However, because Grok used a single self-report rather than 100 fresh sessions, protocol differences and model differences are mixed together.
No. The Grok 4.6 report represents one canonical answer set per test plus 100 simulated draws over uncertain items, whereas Claude and GPT-6 completed 100 independent fresh sessions.
